analysis.title: Middle East Daily, 19 November 2026
key_insights: Oil is steadying after recent losses as markets refocus on Middle East risk. Reports that President Trump is considering a new wave of strikes on Iran put a floor under the selloff, with Brent near USD 92/b and WTI near USD 83/b.
The Brent 1-2 month time spread is USD 2.74/b, which the report describes as supported.
EU natural gas fell 5% overnight to EUR 80.85/MWh, the lowest level since early October.

Weekly EIA data showed a 3.4m bbl build in commercial crude stocks, largely offset by a 3.2m bbl draw in SPR inventories. SPR draws in November have accelerated after two months of more modest declines.
EIA data showed a 5.2m bbl gasoline inventory build, and distillate stockpiles were also higher.
US oil production edged up to slightly above 14m b/d. Crude exports rose 1m b/d last week to 4.5m b/d.
One US aircraft carrier group has left the Middle East, likely heading to Asia per media reports, which slightly lowers the geopolitical temperature.
Gold fell 0.7% overnight to USD 3,856/troy oz after October FOMC minutes showed strong alignment among Fed officials on the need for additional rate hikes.
Commodities more broadly sold off, especially metals, as volatility in AI valuations raises doubts about longer-term demand for copper and other datacentre capital inputs.

GCC credit closed 18 November stabilising but wider. Spreads in investment-grade sovereigns closed +1/3bp as real money resumed selling in the afternoon and stocks sold off into the London close. ETFs flipped to net buyers midday. The report says GCC credit is looking to global macro, which remains risk off.

Saudi central bank FX reserves fell 3.9% m/m in October to USD 447bn, the lowest since October last year and nearly 10% below the March peak of almost USD 500bn. The report estimates more than two years of import cover.
Egypt and the IMF reached a staff-level agreement on a USD 2.3bn disbursement (USD 1.5bn under the EFF, USD 0.8bn under the RSF), taking total IMF finance to Egypt to about USD 10bn.
The IMF projects UAE growth of 0.2% in 2026 and a strong 2027 recovery, helped by oil production estimated to grow 13% next year.
